newsitem.title: TAIWAN: CPC, Osprey to order LNG ship.
newsitem.headline: CPC, Osprey to order LNG ship.

text.p: Taiwan monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Sunday that it and Singaporean partner Osprey Maritime Ltd have decided to jointly buy a liquefied natural gas tanker.

A statement issued by Chinese Petroleum did not say how much it would cost to build the 135,000 cubic-metre ship, but said the state-owned oil firm and Osprey would each invest 40 percent in the LNG vessel.
Monaco-based Gotaas-Larsen Shipping Corp, which was acquired by Osprey in May, would invest the remaining 20 percent, it said.
Chinese Petroleum, Orprey, Gotaas-Larsen would set up a joint-venture -- Faraway Maritime Shipping Co -- to manage the LNG vessel.
The vessel will be made by Japan's Mitsubishi Shipbuilding Corp and is expected to complete by end-1999.
The vessel would be used to ship 1.84 million tonnes of LNG from Indonesia to Taiwan every year.

Chinese Petroleum began importing 1.5 million tonnes of LNG per year from Indonesia in 1990. It has agreed to renew a 20-year contract, which will begin in 1998, to buy 1.84 million tonnes a year of LNG from Indonesia.
Indonesia and Malaysia are Taiwan's only LNG suppliers.
